attempts.label: DANDI:001357
attempts.paper_title: High-Density Recording Reveals Sparse Clusters (But Not Columns) for Shape and Texture Encoding in Macaque V4
attempts.entry_title: Sparse clusters of shape and texture tuning in macaque V4 (Namima et al. 2025)
attempts.summary: The sparse, non-columnar shape clusters and the widespread contrast-invariant tuning held up in this data. The exact counts of clustered neurons and the texture findings did not. Clustered neurons were a minority and levelled off in well-sampled penetrations (21.5% here), but no analysis choice matched the paper's counts, probably because its code is unpublished and its reliability rule is ambiguous. Texture clustering did not reproduce, with a higher clustered fraction than the paper reports (26% to 52%), and the records give no clear cause. The current-source, orientation, curvature and gyral-penetration findings could not be tested, because the files hold only spike times, with no shape images or grid coordinates.
attempts.description: Tests the findings of Namima, Kempkes, Zamarashkina, Owen and Pasupathy (2025) on dandiset 001357, which holds the spike times of Neuropixels units from two monkeys in the shape, texture and position tests. It computes noise-corrected tuning similarity between simultaneously recorded neurons, its decline with distance along the probe (Isimilarity), contrast invariance, and the comparisons across penetrations, textures and stimulus positions. The LF signal, the stimulus images and the penetration coordinates are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Namima et al. (2025) from dandiset 001357

outcomes.notes: The files hold 30 and 44 shape sessions (M1, M2), 17 and 34 texture sessions, and 34 position-test sessions (expected 33 within 3.3; one holds a single unit). 1,869 shape neurons are responsive and 427 excluded, 985 texture neurons responsive and 360 excluded, all within tolerance. The texture files' good units sum to the paper's 1,345 exactly; the shape files hold 2,296 against 2,311.
deviations: Texture responsiveness uses the original and contrast-reversed textures; the spectral-noise version in the files is left out, as the paper does not use it.
Shape responsiveness uses the dark (4 cd/m2) and bright (12 cd/m2) shapes; the files' third luminance level (8 cd/m2) is left out.

outcomes.notes: The files' p06 of M2 (2021-04-14) has 24 responsive neurons spanning 2,340 um; neurons 1 to 9 lie over 540 um and are similarly tuned at both contrasts (mean similarity 0.70 dark, 0.86 bright, against -0.02 with deeper neurons). With dark shapes 13 neurons have a significant positive Isimilarity under both reliability readings, all with negative slopes; neurons 1 to 9 and 14 as in the paper, plus 12, 21 and 22, without 17. Count and set are outside the margin of one neuron. None has a significant negative intercept, so the two-sided count is also 13. With shared noise subtracted the count is 12, within tolerance, but the set lacks 17 and adds 12 and 21.
deviations: Penetrations are found by the files' `pen_ID` label (reading c of the claims file); readings a and b give other sessions whose counts do not match.

Depth is the unit's best-channel position from the files (20 um steps, `depth`, distance from the tip), measured from the most superficial good unit; the template center of mass of the Methods is not in the files.

The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.

The bootstrap resamples each stimulus's repeats (500 times), with the same indices for all neurons of a session. Its distribution sits below the point estimate, since resampling with replacement inflates the noise the estimator corrects for, so the percentile interval is not a confidence interval of the corrected r; only its width decides reliability. Both readings of the reliability rule (width or half-width above 0.5) are run.

The noise of two simultaneously recorded neurons is taken as independent, as in Pospisil and Bair (2021). Their noise correlations are small but positive, largest within 100 um (mean 0.072); a variant subtracts each pair's noise covariance (`nc_corr_shared`).

outcomes.notes: Needs the 120 shape images to compute Gabor filter outputs. The dandiset holds none (`stimulus/templates` is empty) and does not say which shape each stim_ID is. A search for a public, pinned copy of the Pasupathy and Connor (2001) shapes (the shape lab's publication pages, Pospisil et al. 2018 eLife, github.com/deanpospisil/er_est, the SparseShape OSF project) found none; other groups report obtaining them from the lab. A second search, in the final revision, found the outlines of the 370 shapes of the Pasupathy and Connor set at a pinned commit (github.com/deanpospisil/v4cnn, commit b0532e9083eb023c2247e5b53833229e7e6eb740, img_gen/PC3702001ShapeVerts.mat, 401 vertices per shape). The dataset still does not say which 15 of them the shape test used or which stim_ID each is, so the claim stays blocked here; using them needs the 15 shapes of Figure 1B identified in that set and a mapping of stim_ID to them, an analysis left to a new attempt.

With stim_ID 0 as the spindle, 2 of 74 penetrations are all one preference and 2 switch once, so both kinds exist, but M2p6 (horizontal in bins 0 to 5, 0 to 599 um, vertical below, horizontal in its two deepest bins; 2 changes) and M1p5 (12 changes) are of neither kind. Under every stim_ID taken as the spindle, neither penetration is of one kind (M2p6 2 to 12 changes, M1p5 7 to 15), so the outcome does not rest on that mapping.
deviations: The files number shapes 0 to 14 without saying which is the spindle; stim_ID 0 is taken as Shape 1 of Figure 1B, and all 15 are shown.
Rotations 0 and 180 are taken as horizontal, 90 and 270 as vertical (Materials and Methods, Feature models).
Penetrations are found by the files' `pen_ID` label (reading c of the claims file); readings a and b give other sessions whose counts do not match.

985 texture neurons in 51 penetrations (6 to 83 each). No reading puts the counts within tolerance. Original and reversed textures under reliability (a) give 193 and 198 neurons (207) but 30 and 27 penetrations (34), 4 and 2 in M1 (7), and 12 and 7 M1 neurons (18). Reliability (b) gives 276 to 395 neurons in 37 to 42 penetrations. A minority of neurons with a line is clustered under every reading (27% to 41%). Neurons without a line are 304 and 322 under (a) and 62 and 44 under (b), against the paper's 48, which points to reading (b) for the paper's reliability rule. Five M1 texture files (2020-07-15, 07-19, 07-29, 07-30, 08-04) fail the clock check: 9% to 47% of their units fire more on stimuli than on blanks (median 41% across texture files) but 0% to 12% are selective among the textures, so their stimulus labels may not match the presentations. No neuron in them has a line under reliability (a) (original textures), so leaving them out leaves the (a) counts unchanged; under (b) it gives 267 to 379 neurons in 33 to 38 penetrations (7 to 11 in M1). No reading matches either way.

outcomes.notes: 721 shape-responsive neurons in 33 M2 penetrations (723 in the paper) enter the position test (penetrations with 4 or more). Isimilarity at the optimal position against the main shape test with dark shapes (reading b) gives Spearman's r = 0.297 (reliability a, n = 378) and 0.325 (b, n = 676), p below 1e-4. Against the position test's center (reading a), r is 0.447 to 0.474 with the inferred center, p below 1e-4, so with the inferred center every reading gives a positive r with p below 0.0001 and reading (b) is within tolerance. Reading (b) does not use the position labels. Under reliability (b) the five choices of center give r = 0.274 to 0.406, all p below 1e-4, within tolerance only with position 3 (0.329); under (a) 0.279 to 0.567, p below 1e-4 except position 4 (r = 0.279, p = 2.1e-4), which fails the criterion's p below 0.0001. The outcome therefore assumes that the center is not position 4.
deviations: The files code positions 0 to 4 without saying which is the center; the position with the largest mean response of the penetration's responsive neurons is taken as the center (position 1 in 12 files, 2 in 11, 4 in 5, 0 in 3, 3 in 3), and all five are shown. The aggregate RF center is where the stimuli were placed on the neurons' RFs, so the population response should peak there; this is assumed, since the files do not label it. With position 4 as the center under reliability (a), p = 2.1e-4 and the claim would not be reproduced.
Neurons are those responsive in the main shape test; neurons responsive in the position test are a variant (603 neurons, r = 0.298 and 0.348).

Penetrations enter with 4 or more neurons, since a regression line needs 3 other neurons with reliable similarities (Materials and Methods, Clusters of similarly tuned neurons); this follows from the line rule.

outcomes.notes: Under the criterion's rule M2p9 is the session whose responsive count is within 10% of 16, the files' p12 (2021-04-21, 16 neurons); there reading (a) fails for every choice of center and reading (b) finds 0 to 3 neurons with significant Isimilarity per position. Under reliability (a) this is not a test of p12, since only 0 or 1 of its 120 pairs is reliable at each position and no neuron has a line; under reliability (b) it has 13 to 39 reliable pairs. For M2p28 (the files' p28, 55 neurons) reading (b) fails, with up to 2 (reliability a) or 3 to 16 (b) such neurons per position against at most 1. Reading (a) fails for p28 under reliability (a), with position correlations from -0.06 to 1.00 and few reliable pairs (23 to 60 of 1,485), and holds under reliability (b) with position 0 as the center only. With the files' label p09 for M2p9 (18 neurons), reading (b) holds for M2p9 under both reliability readings, and reading (a) holds under reliability (b) for every center and under reliability (a) only with position 1 as the center. So with p09 as M2p9, position 0 as the center and reliability (b), reading (a) holds for both penetrations and reading (b) fails, which the criterion would call blocked; under every other choice both readings fail. Asked whether Figure 11's n is the matrix count, a reader answered that it is (16 and 55 sit with the matrices of panels A and C and Figure 12A; the RF insets read 8 and 26), so the claim and its 10% rule stand and the outcome is unchanged. On the data, the files' p28 has exactly 55 shape-responsive neurons (65 good, 44 responsive in the position test), consistent with matrices of shape-responsive neurons. No count of the files' p09 is within 10% of 16 (20 good, 18 shape-responsive, 12 position-responsive, 12 both, 18 either), so the rule still takes p12 as M2p9. Under that rule reading (b) fails on both p12 and p28 under both reliability readings, and reading (a) fails on p12 for every center under both, so the readings agree and the outcome is not reproduced, not blocked.
deviations: Positions are not labelled; reading (a) is evaluated for every choice of center.

The noise-corrected correlation was written from the Methods' description and Pospisil and Bair (2021) (Materials and Methods, Tuning similarity and contrast invariance); its bias terms are written for unequal repeats per stimulus (3 to 10 here), which reduce to the published terms with equal repeats. The paper's code is not public.

The bootstrap resamples each stimulus's repeats (500 times), with the same indices for all neurons of a session. Its distribution sits below the point estimate, since resampling with replacement inflates the noise the estimator corrects for, so the percentile interval is not a confidence interval of the corrected r; only its width decides reliability. Both readings of the reliability rule (width or half-width above 0.5) are run.

outcomes.notes: A simulation judged by eye, with peak amplitudes and progression step sizes not given, which also needs the shapes' APC descriptions (not public, see apc-peaks-sparse-clustering). It uses no recorded data, so the dataset cannot test it.

findings.statement: The dandiset holds spike times of good units only. The LF signal behind the CSD analysis, the RF-mapping experiment, the stimulus images and the penetrations' grid coordinates are not in it, so the CSD, feature-model and gyral-penetration findings cannot be tested.

Shapes are coded by stim_ID 0 to 14 and the position test's positions 0 to 4 without saying which shape each code is or which position is the aggregate RF center. The position with the largest population response is position 1 in 12 files, 2 in 11, 4 in 5, 0 in 3 and 3 in 3, so the center cannot be read from the data either.
The trial tables of all 34 position-test files give the session as '...SL' (the shape test's code), while their units tables and file names give '...SP'.

The shape files hold a third luminance level, 8 cd/m2 (the background luminance), presented as often as the dark and bright shapes in 73 of 74 files; the paper and the dandiset description mention only dark and bright shapes. The texture files hold the spectral-noise version the description mentions and the paper does not use.

Unit depth is the best channel's distance from the tip in 20 um steps, not the template center of mass the Methods use; it gives the paper's distances for the example pairs (260 and 80 um) and spans (2,340 and 2,580 um).

The Methods say shape and texture tests were run in 34 M2 sessions; the dandiset has 34 M2 texture files of which 29 share a day and penetration label with a shape file, and 5 (p07, p17, p40, p42, p53) are texture-only days. The 2021-05-30 texture file is labelled p40, as is the 2021-05-29 shape file.

The position test has 34 files, where the paper reports 33 sessions; one (2021-05-29, p40) holds a single unit. The shape test of the same day is the penetration with one responsive neuron, where the paper reports at least 6 per penetration.
The texture files do not store the rotation of each presentation, which the Methods say was chosen at random from 8.

Spikes and presentations share a clock in 152 of 159 files (units are tuned to the stimuli at the photodiode onsets and not at onsets moved by -1.3 s). It could not be established in five M1 texture files (2020-07-15, 07-19, 07-29, 07-30, 08-04), where 0% to 12% of units are tuned at the true onsets, nor in the two single-unit files of 2021-05-29. In the five texture files 9% to 47% of units fire more on stimuli than on blanks (median 41% across texture files), so the units respond to stimulus onset but not selectively among the textures, which points to stimulus labels that do not match the presentations.

For the paper's authors. Is a noise-corrected similarity unreliable when the width of its 95% bootstrap interval exceeds 0.5, or its half-width, and what interval level is used? Under the width reading, 1,729 neurons have a regression line with dark shapes and 681 texture neurons with original textures; under the half-width reading 1,805 and 923; the paper has 1,848 and 931. The significant-Isimilarity counts change by 10% to 60% between them. How are unequal repeats per stimulus handled in the bias correction? And what does the estimator give when a neuron's bias-corrected variance is not positive? Here its similarities are undefined, and 62 of the 64 shape neurons without a line under the half-width reading lack one for that reason (the paper has 2).

For the paper's authors. Does the noise-corrected similarity between two simultaneously recorded neurons correct for their noise correlation? Here noise correlations are small but positive and largest for near pairs (mean 0.072 within 100 um, 0.023 beyond 800 um); subtracting them lowers the number of neurons with significant positive Isimilarity from 400 to 274 (dark shapes, width reading) against the paper's 344.

entries.name: 001357-namima-2025
entries.title: Sparse clusters of shape and texture tuning in macaque V4 (Namima et al. 2025)
entries.description: Tests the findings of Namima, Kempkes, Zamarashkina, Owen and Pasupathy (2025) on dandiset 001357, which holds the spike times of Neuropixels units from two monkeys in the shape, texture and position tests. It computes noise-corrected tuning similarity between simultaneously recorded neurons, its decline with distance along the probe (Isimilarity), contrast invariance, and the comparisons across penetrations, textures and stimulus positions. The LF signal, the stimulus images and the penetration coordinates are not in the dandiset.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Namima et al. (2025) from dandiset 001357
